# Fitness functions

Run with `archfit check`. They fail the build when the design breaks one of its own rules.

| ID | Severity | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FIT001 | critical | The catalog must match its schema |
| FIT000 | high | A waiver must not be past its expiry date |
| FIT002 | critical | Every reference in the catalog must resolve |
| FIT003 | high | Dependencies must respect the layering |
| FIT004 | high | No cycles among synchronous or in-process dependencies |
| FIT005 | high | A component may not promise more availability than its hard dependencies allow |
| FIT006 | critical | Data may only flow to components cleared for its classification |
| FIT007 | critical | Only designated egress components may call external systems |
| FIT008 | high | A critical component may not hard-depend on a less critical one |
| FIT009 | high | Tier 1 and 2 components need recovery objectives and a runbook |
| FIT010 | high | Tier 1 components need an owner reachable around the clock |
| FIT011 | medium | Tier 1 and 2 components must emit traces, metrics and logs |
| FIT012 | low | Every component must be used or be an entry point |
| FIT013 | low | Every component needs a unique, well-formed cost tag |

## FIT002: Every reference in the catalog must resolve

**Severity:** critical

**Why it matters.** A dependency, owner, ADR or runbook that does not exist is a gap in the design, not a typo.

**How to fix it.** Fix the id, or add the missing component, team, ADR or runbook.

## FIT003: Dependencies must respect the layering

**Severity:** high

**Why it matters.** Layers exist so that change and failure flow one way. A lower layer calling upward couples the foundation to the products built on it.

**How to fix it.** Move the call behind an interface in an allowed layer, or change the layer rules by ADR.

## FIT004: No cycles among synchronous or in-process dependencies

**Severity:** high

**Why it matters.** A cycle means two components cannot start, deploy or fail independently.

**How to fix it.** Break the cycle with an asynchronous event or by extracting the shared part.

## FIT005: A component may not promise more availability than its hard dependencies allow

**Severity:** high

**Why it matters.** Availability multiplies along a chain of synchronous calls. A target above the product of its dependencies is arithmetically unreachable.

**How to fix it.** Lower the target, add a fallback, make the call optional or asynchronous, or raise the dependency.

## FIT006: Data may only flow to components cleared for its classification

**Severity:** critical

**Why it matters.** Sending restricted data to a component cleared only for confidential data is a classification breach, whatever the reason.

**How to fix it.** Redact before the call, route to a component cleared for the class, or reclassify with approval.

## FIT007: Only designated egress components may call external systems

**Severity:** critical

**Why it matters.** Every outbound path to a model provider or SaaS API is a place data can leave. Keeping the set small is what makes policy, logging and cost control complete.

**How to fix it.** Route the call through an egress component, or designate the component as egress by ADR.

## FIT008: A critical component may not hard-depend on a less critical one

**Severity:** high

**Why it matters.** A tier 1 service that cannot run without a tier 3 service is really tier 3.

**How to fix it.** Raise the dependency's tier and its obligations, add a fallback, or make the call optional.

## FIT009: Tier 1 and 2 components need recovery objectives and a runbook

**Severity:** high

**Why it matters.** If nobody has written down how fast it must come back and how, it will be decided during an outage.

**How to fix it.** Set rto_minutes and rpo_minutes within policy and add the runbook.

## FIT010: Tier 1 components need an owner reachable around the clock

**Severity:** high

**Why it matters.** A critical component owned by a business-hours team is unowned at 3 a.m.

**How to fix it.** Give the owning team a pager rotation, or move ownership.

## FIT011: Tier 1 and 2 components must emit traces, metrics and logs

**Severity:** medium

**Why it matters.** A component you cannot observe cannot meet an SLO you cannot measure.

**How to fix it.** Declare the telemetry the component emits, and emit it.

## FIT012: Every component must be used or be an entry point

**Severity:** low

**Why it matters.** A component nothing depends on is cost and attack surface with no purpose in the design.

**How to fix it.** Remove it, connect it, or mark it as an entrypoint.

## FIT013: Every component needs a unique, well-formed cost tag

**Severity:** low

**Why it matters.** Showback and unit economics need every cost attributed to exactly one component.

**How to fix it.** Give the component a distinct kebab-case cost_tag.
